beats: Hook: a thousand GPUs each finish their homework with a different answer; how do they all get the class total without one doing everyone's sums? (line_allreduce_one_desk, line_dog_homework)

Data parallel recap: copy the model, shard the data, each copy gets a different gradient; sum them and it is as if one GPU saw the whole batch (slides 31-33) (line_split_twin_kitchens, pre-drawn for L04-03).
AllReduce: everyone ends with the same sum (slide 34) (line_allreduce_same_sheet).

Ring, part 1: tear each answer sheet into N strips (line_allreduce_tear_strips); reduce-scatter: everyone passes one strip right and adds, N-1 steps (slides 35-37) (line_allreduce_desk_circle, line_allreduce_add_two).
Ring, part 2: all-gather, the finished strips go round again, N-1 steps; 2(N-1) steps of M/N each (slides 38-40) (line_allreduce_chef_ring as a chef-cast variant).
Tree: pairs add and pass up, the top broadcasts down: 2 log N steps, but each moves the full M (slides 41-42) (line_allreduce_pyramid, line_allreduce_megaphone).
Ring vs tree: bandwidth for big gradients vs latency for small control data (slide 43) (line_allreduce_postcard_train).
Pitfall: one slow link sets the pace of every ring step (900 vs 50 GB/s) (line_cluster_kitchen_street, pre-drawn for L04-02).
Hierarchy: reduce-scatter inside the node on NVLink, cross nodes with quarter-size pieces, all-gather inside (slide 44; L05 4-5) (line_allreduce_two_rooms). Takeaway.
